displayPattern: Amber LED on a Bryant 80% two-stage variable-speed furnace (troubleshooting guide TG-GFB80-02). Short flashes are the first digit and long flashes are the second. Code 25 is 2 short and 5 long
meaning: Model selection or setup error. The model plug PL4 is missing or incorrect, or setup switch SW1-1 or SW1-6 is in the wrong position. If 25 flashes only four times at power-up, the control is using the model stored in memory.
causes: Model plug PL4 missing or incorrect
A heating or cooling call is present while SW1-1 is ON
A heating or cooling call is present while SW1-6 is ON
SW1-1 and SW1-6 are both ON
Two different furnace models are twinned
diySteps: Count whether 25 flashes four times and stops, or keeps flashing. Four times means the control defaulted to the stored model. Continuous flashing is the rest of the list
Turn SW1-1 off after you finish reading stored codes. The recall procedure in this guide uses SW1-1, and leaving it on is one cause of code 25
Technician: compare the model plug number and resistance with the wiring diagram
safetyNote: If you smell gas, do not touch any electrical switch or use a phone in the building; leave immediately and call your gas supplier from outside. Turn off electrical power at the furnace switch or breaker before opening any panel, and never bypass or jumper a limit, rollout or pressure switch. Gas valve, burner, venting, wiring and control-board work should be done by a licensed HVAC technician.
proAdvice: Call a licensed HVAC technician if 25 keeps flashing after the setup switches are off and the model plug is seated. Do not twin two different models.
sourceTitle: Bryant 80% variable-speed two-stage furnace troubleshooting guide (Catalog No. TG-GFB80-02)
